It is traditionally used for rheumatism, boils. The leaves are the most commonly used part, usually prepared as a herbal tea. Reported properties include antioxidant, antibacterial activity.
dosage: Herbal tea: steep 2 tsp of dried leaves in hot water, drink twice daily.
contraindications: Prolonged high-dose use may cause loose stools; May cause allergic skin reaction in sensitive individuals
source: Indigenous Medicine Field Notes Vol. II
